results.content:
Find out more

## Why this story matters

OpenAI has launched a restricted version of ChatGPT specifically for users ages 13 to 17, with built-in limits on content and chatbot behavior that differ from the standard platform.

### Content is filtered by default

The teen version automatically blocks content related to self-harm, violence, eating disorders and explicit sexual material, according to OpenAI.

### Homework help is restricted

The platform is designed to guide teens through problems rather than provide direct answers, limiting how the tool can be used for schoolwork.

### Emotional engagement is limited

OpenAI says the chatbot is prohibited from using romantic language, encouraging emotional dependence or implying it has feelings or consciousness. [...] Forbes Georgia

### What’s different

OpenAI says if users don’t sign up as teens, but its age-prediction system estimates a user is one, they will be automatically placed into ChatGPT for Teens. The platform’s default settings are meant to “reduce exposure to content that may be harmful or developmentally inappropriate” for teens.

It will filter out content centered on self-harm, violence, eating disorders, dangerous activities, and explicit sexual or graphic content, according to OpenAI.

SAN FRANCISCO -- OpenAI is launching a version of ChatGPT designed for teenagers — the first generation to grow up with artificial intelligence — who are already using it for schoolwork, questions about daily life and even companionship.

The San Francisco-based company says ChatGPT for Teens, which launches Tuesday, is tailored for kids aged 13 to 17 with stronger protections including content restrictions around things like suicide, self-harm and romantic or sexual chats. It also provides homework and study support designed to help students learn rather than spit out answers and school essays.

## Four tests for any AI a child uses

 Content: moderated for a child’s age — not adult-standard safety bolted on.
 Data: child-privacy by design, so a parent can review and delete.
 Network: closed — no open web, no ads, no rabbit holes.
 Thinking: makes a child reason instead of handing over the answer — the test most general tools fail.

## The options parents weigh

### ChatGPT (OpenAI)

General-purpose AI assistant

Best for: Open-ended help, writing, and brainstorming for teens and adults.

OpenAI’s terms set a minimum age of 13, and under-18s need a parent’s permission. There’s no child-calibrated moderation, no parent view of conversations, and it can reach the open web — so for under-13s it means supervising an adult tool.

### Google Gemini

General-purpose AI assistant [...] ### Google Gemini

General-purpose AI assistant

Best for: General help across Google’s apps, for older students and adults.

Google offers teen access with family-management controls, but like other general assistants it isn’t designed specifically for 7–11-year-olds, nor built around a child’s privacy and a parent’s view of learning.

### Khanmigo (Khan Academy)

Curriculum tutor

Best for: Structured, curriculum-aligned tutoring and school-topic mastery, in a Socratic, guide-don’t-tell style.

Genuinely strong for academic practice. It lives inside Khan’s web platform rather than a closed, age-built space — an excellent complement to a thinking-first companion.
